About The Role
We are actively seeking a Data Platform Engineer to join our team and play a pivotal role in building and evolving our modern cloud data platform. This platform is integral to powering analytics, internal applications, automation, and AI initiatives across the organization. The ideal candidate will have a strong foundation in data engineering, with a focus on designing scalable pipelines, developing data models, and ensuring high data quality. 3+ years of experience in Data Engineering, Platform Engineering, Cloud Engineering, or a related field
Strong proficiency in Python and SQL
Hands-on experience with Snowflake or other cloud data warehouses
Experience with Git and CI/CD pipelines
Familiarity with workflow orchestration tools such as Airflow or similar
Experience with serverless computing, particularly AWS Lambda or equivalent

Description
Do you want to directly influence the experience of your most critical customers? Does providing creative solutions to complex technology problems motivate you? Worldwide Operations Security is seeking a pioneer to help build a world-class video analytics and security infrastructure for our fulfillment teams across the globe.
We are looking for a Systems Development Engineer to develop video analytics functionality and create innovative video security solutions built upon leading AI engines such as Amazon Bedrock and Rekognition. You will be responsible for designing and building systems to deploy, maintain, and extend our internal video capabilities globally. This position will include the development and implementation of internally written software for highly specialized analytics systems, application deployment, and support. You will use AWS products and DevOps patterns to build this next generation of video tools.
The candidate we're seeking is a motivated builder who drives innovation and will deliver results to our customers. This is a hands-on position where your daily activities will range from strategic planning to new system development to supporting the customers that depend on your services. You will deliver consistent, well-defined results in an agile development workflow. To succeed in this role, you will deliver on-time results that delight your customers while inspiring your team to think big about their work. If this sounds like a fit, we would love to speak with you.
Key job responsibilities
Create and maintain cloud-based video analytics solutions for use by internal stakeholders.
Create and maintain cloud-based automation applications for the deployment and configuration of 1P and 3P video solutions
Continuously strive for operational excellence by seeking to provide cost-effective and highly available solutions.
Participate in original creation and implementation of scalable infrastructure automation tools that allow Amazon to get the most out of our global Operations video security infrastructure.
Ensure that all products are designed to be secure, robust, scalable, maintainable and adaptable as the services scale and evolve over time.
Build instrumentation to provide visibility into the health of your products, along with alerting and self-healing capabilities.
Uphold a high standard of code quality and engineering excellence.
A day in the life
Our team develops analytics and automation tools using AWS services and internal AI platforms to provide video solutions to our internal security and safety teams. We use Agile Scrum to track our project work, conducting biweekly sprint planning meetings and 3 standup meetings a week to coordinate efforts. We work closely with our internal stakeholders in the Loss Prevention, Operations, and Safety organizations. Typical project work includes creating new solutions based on customer requirements for expanding video system capabilities. Typical operations work includes providing escalation support for anything that the front-line support team requires assistance with.
About The Team
The security video solutions in use at Amazon sites are critical tools for ensuring the safety of Amazon associates and the security of our facilities. Our team's vision is to ensure that our video applications and infrastructure are easy to deploy, configured appropriately at each site, highly available, and used to their full potential. We're a collaborative engineering team who overlap in responsibilities and project work. Plan to spend time working will teammates on building new tools for making our vision a reality, and on coordinating closely with stakeholders to learn their needs and deliver the results they're looking for.
Basic Qualifications
Experience in automating, deploying, and supporting infrastructure
Experience programming with at least one modern language such as Python, Ruby, Golang, Java, C++, C#, Rust
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Systems Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or other related discipline
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with CI/CD pipelines build processes
Experience with distributed systems at scale
Experience in networking, storage systems, operating systems and hands-on systems engineering

description_preview:
About Smack
Smack is building domain-specific models for the sole purpose of delivering AI-enabled decision-making for modern warfare. Our team has decades of military leadership experience at every level. We understand the problem better than anyone, and we know exactly what our end users need to solve it.
About the Role
We’re pushing Smack’s domain-specific models to the tactical edge, orchestrating decision-making in denied, disrupted, intermittent, and limited (DDIL) comms environments. We treat RF as both a comms link and an environment sensor, where you’ll work at the intersection of unique technical problems and impactful missions.
The real world is right; your model of it is wrong. We emphasize fast feedback loops that enable us to move from concept to fielded system rapidly. Your job is to own the RF and communications edge architecture from system design to physical deployment. You will deploy onto edge-deployed hardware, ensuring our decision-making systems operate under comms and sensing degradation gracefully and within deployed constraints.
This role is ideal for engineers who want a high-ownership, fast-moving startup environment and who can bridge signal theory and real-world data to create impact quickly.
What You’ll Do
Architect and field resilient comms: design, build, and deploy end-to-end RF and communications architectures tailored for tactical edge hardware
Characterize link reliability and RF situational awareness in DDIL environments, building systems that degrade gracefully under heavy jamming or signal loss
Bridge signal processing and SDR hardware: deploy ML and signal processing algorithms onto software-defined radios and edge devices
Build high-throughput, low-latency DSP pipelines using C++, Python, and/or GNU Radio, treating RF as a dual-use asset for both tactical communications and spectrum sensing
Validate from lab bench to live field, using spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and oscilloscopes, etc., alongside realistic field testing
Run field trials to understand when our systems fail, and feed real-world data back into the models
Required Skills
B.S. or M.S. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, Physics, or a related technical discipline (or equivalent practical work experience), with experience writing production-grade code

About Us
MintMCP
helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.
Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. MintMCP scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.
We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.
AI-Native Startup
We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team, write code, review PRs, and handle sales, marketing, and deal ops on the same gateway we sell to customers. We are building an entire company operating system around them, and you will help build it.
Traction
Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 40+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.
The Job
You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.
Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.

About You

You have strong fundamentals and learn fast. How quickly you pick things up matters as much as years of experience.
You care about product value and customer needs over technical purity.
You take infra seriously. You think about blast radius, trust boundaries, and what happens when your code is in the path of every customer's agents.
You can read unfamiliar code, reason from first principles, and explain your tradeoffs.

Developer-facing products, protocol or gateway work, or infrastructure at scale.
Background in security, identity, or permission systems.
Contributions to open source, MCP servers, or agentic frameworks.
Design sensibility: engineers who care about design, designers who think about infrastructure.

Competitive compensation and meaningful equity.
Unusual scope and ownership of features that ship to enterprise customers.
Building and deploying agents on the same platform we sell.
Direct access to the founders, customer context, and product direction, with mentorship as you grow.
Health benefits, on a team that puts family and health first.

Materials Engineer I, R&D and Process Development

Belmont, North Carolina, Charlotte Area

Full-Time

Entry Level

On-Site
Visa Sponsorship:
Available for qualified candidates
About LTS Research Laboratories
LTS Research Laboratories, Inc. is a materials technology company specializing in high-purity materials, advanced inorganic materials, rare-earth materials, sputtering targets, evaporation materials, and custom materials for research and industrial applications.
We are seeking an
Entry-Level Materials Engineer
who is interested in hands-on research, materials processing, chemical development, powder metallurgy, and advanced materials characterization.
This is a laboratory and manufacturing-focused position. The successful candidate will work directly with new materials, experimental processes, analytical instruments, and production equipment rather than working exclusively at a desk.
Position Summary
The Materials Engineer will support research and development of new chemical compounds and advanced materials and assist in developing processes to convert raw materials and powders into finished products.
The position will involve materials including metals, alloys, ceramics, inorganic compounds, rare-earth compounds, organometallic materials, and selected specialty chemicals.
A major focus of the position will be developing and optimizing processes for manufacturing
sputtering targets, pellets, powders, granules, and other advanced material forms
.
Key Responsibilities
Conduct R&D on new inorganic, rare-earth, organometallic, and specialty chemical materials.
Develop and optimize synthesis, purification, heat-treatment, and materials-processing procedures.
Develop processes for manufacturing sputtering targets from powders, including powder preparation, blending, particle-size control, pressing, sintering, heat treatment, density evaluation, grinding, and finishing.
Operate laboratory and production-scale powder presses and assist with development of pressing parameters for pellets and sputtering targets.
Investigate the relationship between powder characteristics, pressing conditions, sintering parameters, density, microstructure, and final material performance.
Prepare experimental batches and scale successful laboratory processes toward production.
Characterize raw materials, intermediate materials, and finished products using techniques including:
X-Ray Diffraction (XRD)
Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM)
Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDS)
Particle Size Distribution (PSD)
ICP-MS
Other chemical and materials characterization techniques as required
Interpret analytical results and determine whether materials meet purity, phase, particle-size, density, and compositional requirements.
Investigate material failures, contamination, oxidation, phase changes, processing problems, and other technical issues.
Work with high-temperature furnaces, vacuum equipment, powder-processing equipment, presses, laboratory instruments, and related manufacturing equipment.
Handle air-sensitive, moisture-sensitive, hygroscopic, reactive, and high-purity materials using appropriate laboratory procedures and inert-atmosphere techniques when required.
Maintain accurate laboratory notebooks, experimental records, processing parameters, and analytical data.
Prepare technical reports, specifications, test reports, Certificates of Analysis, and internal process documentation.
Develop and improve standard operating procedures for laboratory and manufacturing processes.
Support incoming raw-material qualification and finished-product quality control.
Assist with technical evaluation of customer specifications and custom material requirements.
Work closely with production, quality, technical sales, and management to transition successful R&D projects into repeatable manufacturing processes.
Maintain laboratory safety, cleanliness, chemical labeling, proper material storage, and compliance with established safety procedures.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in
Materials Science and Engineering, Materials Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Ceramic Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering
, or a closely related technical field.
Strong fundamental understanding of materials science, chemistry, and materials characterization.
Interest in hands-on laboratory, R&D, and manufacturing work.
Ability to analyze experimental data and troubleshoot technical problems.
Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate technical documentation.
Ability to safely work with chemicals, powders, laboratory equipment, furnaces, vacuum systems, and manufacturing equipment.
Basic computer skills including Microsoft Excel, Word, and technical data analysis.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Previous industrial experience is
not required. New graduates are encouraged to apply.
Experience through university laboratories, internships, research projects, or previous employment in any of the following areas is desirable:
Powder metallurgy
Ceramic processing
Sputtering targets
Thin-film materials
Powder pressing and pelletization
Sintering
High-temperature furnaces
Vacuum processing
Glovebox or inert-atmosphere processing
XRD
SEM/EDS
Particle-size analysis
ICP-MS or other elemental-analysis techniques
Rare-earth materials
High-purity metals and compounds
Materials synthesis
Materials failure analysis
Experimental and statistical data analysis
M.S. in Materials Science, Materials Engineering, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related field is a plus, but is not required.
Compensation & Benefits
LTS Research Laboratories offers a competitive compensation and benefits package for full-time employees, including:
Competitive salary
401(k) retirement plan
Health insurance benefits
Paid time off (PTO)
Paid vacation
Paid sick leave
Paid company holidays
Professional development and hands-on technical training

Job Summary
The Software Engineer II designs, develops, tests, implements, and supports enterprise healthcare applications running on the IBM i platform. This position works with RPG, CL, Db2 for i, SQL, stored procedures, and related technologies to deliver reliable, maintainable solutions that comply with established architecture, quality, security, and engineering standards.
The engineer participates throughout the software development lifecycle, including requirements analysis, technical design, estimation, coding, testing, implementation, documentation, and production support. This role also identifies opportunities to improve application architecture and engineering processes, collaborates with cross-functional teams, and provides technical guidance to less-experienced developers. The existing position requires experience developing complex applications, knowledge of SDLC practices, relational database concepts, design patterns, testing, and configuration management.
Salary: 90K - 120K
What Your Impact Will Be
Develop and maintain programs using RPG, ILE RPG, free-form RPG, CL, Db2 for i, embedded SQL, SQL procedures, and user-defined functions.
Produce technical designs that follow established architecture, database, security, and coding standards.
Analyze business and technical requirements; translate them into effective software solutions.
Design, develop, test, debug, implement, and maintain applications on the IBM i platform.
Provide accurate estimates for assigned work and communicate risks, dependencies, and changes that may affect delivery commitments.
Create and execute unit, integration, system, regression, and performance testing as appropriate.
Diagnose and resolve application defects, data issues, production incidents, and performance problems.
Participate in code reviews, technical design reviews, and architecture discussions.
Maintain technical documentation, implementation instructions, and operational support materials.
Collaborate with product management, quality assurance, operations, database administration, architecture, and other engineering teams.
Participate in Agile planning, backlog refinement, daily stand-ups, demonstrations, and retrospectives.
Use approved source-control, change-management, build, deployment, and AI-assisted development tools in accordance with company policies.
Identify deficiencies in applications, technical designs, and engineering processes and recommend practical improvements.
Support application modernization efforts, including the replacement or refactoring of legacy components.
Provide technical guidance and mentoring to junior engineers when needed.
Assist with production support, troubleshooting, and root-cause analysis.
Complete assigned work in accordance with established schedules, regulatory requirements, and organizational priorities.
Maintain compliance with the MEDHOST Quality Management System and applicable regulatory requirements.
Perform other duties as required to support the needs of the organization.
These responsibilities retain the core expectations in the current job description, including solution design, estimation, process improvement, technical guidance, schedule accountability, and QMS compliance.
What We're Looking For
A bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, Software Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
Five or more years of commercial software-development experience.
Professional experience developing and supporting applications on IBM i.
Experience with RPG, ILE RPG, free-form RPG, and CL.
Experience with Db2 for i and SQL.
Experience developing or supporting SQL stored procedures, functions, views, triggers, or other database objects.
Understanding of relational database concepts, data modeling, normalization, indexing, and query optimization.
Experience working within a structured software development lifecycle.
Experience with source control, configuration management, and formal change-management processes.
Understanding of software design principles, modular development, reusable components, and established design patterns.
Experience with unit, integration, system, regression, and performance testing.
Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively within a development team.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to document technical designs, decisions, procedures, and implementation requirements.
The current description establishes the baseline of five or more years of product-development experience, RPG and CL, Db2 SQL, SQL procedures, testing knowledge, analytical ability, technical writing, and change-management experience.
What Will Make You Stand Out
Experience with modern RPG development practices and fully free-form RPG.
Experience with Git-based source control and contemporary IBM i development tools.
Experience using Visual Studio Code or Rational Developer for i.
Experience with REST APIs, JSON, XML, web services, or application integration.
Experience modernizing legacy IBM i applications.
Experience with healthcare software, revenue-cycle applications, financial systems, or other regulated enterprise environments.
Familiarity with Agile or Scrum development practices.
Experience with production support and root-cause analysis.
Experience using approved AI-assisted software-development tools.
Familiarity with Java, HTML, JavaScript, or other cross-platform technologies.

description_preview:
Description
Who We Are:
Kudu Dynamics is a 100% employee-owned company, forged out of a decade of experience in computer network operations and staffed with talent who have built, overseen, and enhanced capabilities throughout the entire USG arsenal. Our team of hackers, engineers, makers, and shakers brings deep experience across research, development, deployment, and operations.
Kudu Dynamics is uniquely qualified to anticipate tomorrow’s threats and build the next generation of capabilities.
When you come in for your interview, you’ll see that Kudu is an amazing place to work, where you’ll be surrounded by experts who are ready to teach and learn. Our team has flexible work hours and work-from-home options. When we do work from the offices, we enjoy home-roasted coffee and award-winning workspaces.
Job Description
Hello! We’re a small team in a fun company looking for someone to come in and help us build systems that stay reliable when things get complicated.
We need a Site Reliability Engineer who has experience building, deploying, automating, and operating complex compute platforms. You’ll work across infrastructure, Linux systems, networking, distributed storage, observability, security, and deployment automation, with a particular emphasis on creating systems that are reproducible, maintainable, resilient, and easy to operate.
A major part of this role will involve Nix and NixOS. We want someone who appreciates declarative systems, reproducible environments, infrastructure-as-code, and reducing configuration drift. You may be building NixOS-based servers, improving deployment pipelines, developing reusable Nix modules, debugging distributed systems, or making sure a platform can be rebuilt predictably from scratch.
Critical components of the environment may include high-performance compute, distributed Linux file systems, network design, security-in-depth, ML/AI infrastructure, high-bandwidth data processing, cloud deployment, and fielded systems.
You don’t need to be an expert at everything. Whatever part you bite off, though, will be yours to own. This is a great opportunity to apply deep systems expertise while learning adjacent areas.
Our team needs your help making sure our customers are repeatedly provided with operational insights from a multi-domain data environment—and that the infrastructure producing those insights is dependable, observable, reproducible, and recoverable.
These Are The Things You’ll Get To Do
Own the reliability and operation of critical compute and data platforms.
Design, deploy, and maintain Linux infrastructure, including NixOS-based systems.
Build reproducible system configurations and deployment workflows using Nix and infrastructure-as-code.
Develop reusable NixOS modules, packages, flakes, and system configurations.
Improve platform resilience, fault tolerance, recoverability, and maintainability.
Build monitoring, logging, alerting, and observability capabilities that help us understand system behavior before customers notice problems.
Diagnose difficult failures across Linux, networking, storage, containers, and distributed systems.
Automate repetitive operational tasks and eliminate configuration drift.
Design and build security and maintainability components for deployed systems.
Help define operational standards, deployment practices, upgrade strategies, and disaster-recovery procedures.
Perform capacity planning and identify performance bottlenecks across compute, storage, and networking.
Own solutions spanning CNO, analytics, security, infrastructure, and field deployments.
Learn new skills and teach the rest of us what you know.
Minimum Qualifications
Enthusiasm for learning new stuff.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, a related field, or amazing equivalent skills.
Strong experience administering and troubleshooting Linux systems.
Experience with Linux networking, storage, and file systems.
Experience automating system configuration and deployment.
Experience with Nix and/or NixOS in production, lab, or significant personal environments.
Python, Go, Bash, or similar scripting/programming experience of 2+ years.
Ability to debug complex systems methodically across multiple layers of the stack.
Nice-to-Have Qualifications
Deep experience with NixOS, including custom modules, overlays, flakes, packaging, and reproducible deployments.
Experience operating fleets of Linux systems.
Infrastructure-as-code experience with Nix, Terraform, Ansible, or similar tooling.
Experience designing highly available or fault-tolerant systems.
Monitoring and observability experience with tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, OpenTelemetry, Elasticsearch, or similar systems.

description_preview:
We’re looking for a Software Engineer to join our Devops Platform team, where you will blend linux system administration and software engineering skills to build and maintain all our infrastructure and core services running in our data centers and the cloud.
Wealthfront’s Infrastructure team is a team of “Generalists with Expertise” who adhere to DevOps principles by building software and services to automate all infrastructure operations. Our objective is to empower all our developers to build and own their systems end-to-end.
We're a modern infrastructure engineering team, believing strongly in testing, automation, and standardization through software. We operate in both physical data centers and AWS environments, and leverage open source technologies such as containers, MariaDB, NGINX, Jenkins, and Chef, as well as build tools and services using Go and Java to deliver automated infrastructure to our engineers and ultimately serve our clients.
About Wealthfront Engineering
Wealthfront’s culture centers around continuous learning, innovation, and quality-driven software development. With high quality software as our ultimate engineering objective, our key tactic is automation:
•
Wealthfront software automates the financial services we provide to our clients, and within these services we automate the collection of data that we learn from on our way to making our services even better.
•
Wealthfront engineers function as builder/operators, with dual responsibility for building the system and operating it in production. Any toil that this brings about is automated away by engineers. This investment in automation is expected, and the prioritization of it is always built into our planning and execution.
•
Wealthfront engineers automate our development processes. For example, Wealthfront engineers automate all of our testing. Manual testing is not part of the software development lifecycle at Wealthfront.
•
Wealthfront engineers automate observability in case of failure. If something is up, our systems inform engineers appropriately. If our systems are quiet, they are healthy.
If you are drawn to being an engineer within such an environment, and having outsized impact as an engineer at a magnitude that is only available within a company achieving greatness at our size (~350 employees, half in engineering), then we want to hear from you!
As a member of the team, you will:
Maintain our core infrastructure by writing software to automate application deployment, configure our infrastructure, and manage critical services such as our databases.
Ensure that mission critical services operate reliably by triaging and fixing operational issues in linux environments as an on-call engineer, participating in post-mortems, and implementing improvements to prevent future issues.
Design, implement, and deploy internal tools and services to accelerate productivity of the wider Engineering team and enable direct ownership of operations.
Help manage our server hardware in our physical data centers which may occasionally include travel to our Bay Area or New Jersey data centers for onsite projects.
Be involved in key decisions regarding the evolution of our infrastructure
This role could be a fit if you have:
A BS or MS in Computer Science or an Engineering field
Experience with running and troubleshooting modern Linux systems and services in production
2+ years of experience developing reliable production-grade software in Java, Go, or other similar languages
Proficiency with at least one automation technology such as Terraform, Chef, or Puppet
Successfully designed and deployed mission-critical complex distributed systems
Excellent critical thinking and communications skills with a desire to both learn from and educate your peers
Once you join, Wealthfront will:
Pair you with a 1:1 mentor to guide you through our onboarding program.
Encourage you to lead impactful projects which match your professional goals.
Support your professional development by providing feedback during weekly 1:1s and during our bi-annual reviews.
Be given the opportunity to participate in designing systems and planning for the future of our infrastructure
Estimated annual salary range: $150,000 - $189,000 plus equity and a discretionary bonus.
Benefits include medical, vision, dental, 401K plan, generous time off, parental leave, wellness reimbursements, professional development, employee investing discount, and more!
